create.name: Appamada
create.bio:
Appamada is a contemporary Zen centre in Austin, Texas, housed in a small house on East 38th Street just north of the University of Texas campus. Its name is a Pali word for heedful, energetic care. The community grew out of a Sunday sitting group formed in 1995, began meeting at co-founder Peg Syverson's home in 2005, and only adopted the name Appamada in 2009. Its roots run through two streams of American Zen: the Soto lineage of Shunryu Suzuki, through training at Austin Zen Center, and the everyday-life teaching of Charlotte Joko Beck, with whom Syverson studied for about twenty years. Today it is guided by three senior teachers, Peg Syverson, Flint Sparks and Nate Smalley, together with several lay entrusted teachers.

Weekday mornings begin with zazen and a short service, and Sunday mornings bring an orientation for newcomers, sitting and a Dharma talk. A practice the centre calls Inquiry, in which a teacher meets one person's real question in front of the group, runs each week, as do study and sharing circles, and practice meetings with teachers are available on request. Almost everything is also on Zoom. Daily sitting and talks are freely offered, while some intensives and classes carry a fee, and hundreds of talks are posted to its YouTube channel.

courses.title: Ways to Practice: daily zazen, Sunday mornings and weekly circles
courses.description: Weekday zazen at 6:30 and 7:05 am with a short service, a Sunday morning of orientation, sitting and a Dharma talk, and weekly gatherings such as Inquiry, Depth in Practice and Zazen and Sharing, in Austin and on Zoom.
courses.price: Daily zazen, dharma talks, and weekly programs are freely offered

courses.title: Meet with a Teacher
courses.description: Twenty-minute practice discussions with one of Appamada's senior or entrusted teachers, during morning and Sunday sitting or online on request, plus informal conversations with experienced sangha members who serve as Zen mentors.

free_resources.title: Principles of Meditation
free_resources.description: An archived class by Peg Syverson that goes deeper than a first orientation, covering concentration practice, shikantaza, walking and work meditation, with downloadable handouts and readings.

free_resources.title: Zazen Instruction
free_resources.description: Plain guidance on sitting meditation at Appamada: how to take a seat on cushion, bench or chair, how to hold the hands and eyes, and how to stay with restlessness rather than move away from it.

free_resources.title: Recordings: Dharma talks, Inquiry and intensives
free_resources.description: Links to the centre's recorded Sunday talks, Inquiry sessions and intensive teachings, posted as videos on YouTube and as audio files on SoundCloud.

free_resources.title: Writings: essays from Appamada's teachers
free_resources.description: Downloadable essays by the teachers on how the community took shape and on practice itself, with titles such as Enough, Persistence, Spiritual Friendship and Zen Training: Mindfulness Is Not Enough.

'Erin's Final Teachings' also left out (unclear subject).

Flint Sparks is described as a former psychologist; Appamada's teaching draws on psychology and the class archive includes Hakomi and Internal Family Systems series. The centre itself is a Zen practice community, not a therapy practice; those classes were not listed.
